partial: AC-08.4.3 names specific excluded derived values (insurance start date, civil status for fund/source tax, source-tax subject, tariff code) that the cited facts never mention, since they only say "nothing more".

The step notes put the source tax details (denomination, spouse works, children: steps 6/6a) before the cross-border questions (step 7). A Liechtenstein resident who returns daily, or expects at most 45 non-return days, gets 'in principle no source tax liability' and no tariff code. So their denomination, spouse employment and children answers are not needed (AC-05.7.3 shows them as '–'). Should these employees be asked the Liechtenstein questions first and then skip denomination, spouse employment and children? Or are those answers asked and then discarded on submission? Either way the order of the flow changes, and so does what is collected (G-01 data minimisation).

Is the email address typed in for the copy recorded for HR or kept after the email is sent, or only used to send it? Does the copy itself list the 'send me a copy' answer and the email address as submitted answers? The spec says 'nothing more' but does not say whether these two closing items count as answers.

What date checks apply? Can the first working day be in the past, or how far in the future? Is there a minimum or maximum age for the employee's date of birth, and any check on the spouse's date of birth? The ACs only say 'required, DD.MM.YYYY'. A wrong first working day directly gives a wrong insurance start date.

The rule 'How a child counts for the tariff' and the Single-parent H rule say a child counts as an H child when it 'lives in the household and the employee has sole custody or is the main contributor'. Yet row 21 (and AC-06.3.3) count a minor child NOT in the household as an H child (single parent with custody, alternating care, employee is the main contributor → H1N). Which is right: the plain-language rule or the decision table? The H/P letter depends on it.

"are derived again from the latest answers; no history of earlier values is kept" - This makes a storage/retention decision for all derived results. The source (D-033) only says no history is kept of earlier first working days; the spec's own trace check notes this extension is not backed.

"The expression evaluates one child; the rule applies to each child." - It refers to an implementation artifact (an 'expression') instead of the business rule. The same applies to 'The expression covers a single child; with several children the counts are added up.'

"Lonio records that the tariff code cannot be computed yet instead of a possibly wrong code, so the case stays visible for HR" - This prescribes system behaviour that no stakeholder or decision asked for; the trace check says the cited facts do not require it. The open question still offers 'HR determines the code' as an alternative.

"the employee can add further children and remove a child, and the child questions repeat per child" - This describes interaction mechanics (add/remove child blocks, copied from the calculator UI). The business need is only that each child's answers are collected; how the employee enters several children is a UI choice.

info.message: The certificate of residence question is phrased two ways. information.md asks whether the employee 'has' a certificate; AC-07.2.2 asks whether they 'have provided' it (to HR). Which one is meant? An employee who has the certificate but has not handed it in yet would answer differently, and the answer switches between the cross-border and normal tariff.

The cross-border answers are 'what they expect for the year' / 'in the calendar year'. Which year is meant for an employee who starts late in the year (e.g. in December): the current calendar year, the first full year, or the next 12 months? Without this the question wording cannot be finalised.

For Liechtenstein residents with more than 45 non-return days, the normal code is 'marked subject to the double taxation agreement'. Is this case also flagged for HR, like the 'in principle no liability' case? Or is it only a note on the code? Two different outcomes have to be recorded.
Is there a maximum number of children an employee can enter? The calculator limit is unknown, and the tariff code holds a single digit. What should the result be when 10 or more children count?

For married employees, 'Has children' includes the spouse's/partner's children. For a stepchild, whose custody, maintenance contribution and 'other parent' do the custody and contribution questions refer to? The question wording has to make this clear, or answers will be inconsistent.
HR words the permit reminder. Who supplies the final text, and by when? It also has to work for Swiss citizens living abroad. Without the text the story cannot be finished or accepted.

Before submission, can the employee leave the questionnaire and come back later with their answers kept? Is there a deadline, or a point at which an unsubmitted questionnaire's answers are deleted? 'Kept while going back and forth' does not say whether answers survive across sessions, which matters for data minimisation.

Should the employee see the derived insurance start date (or the source tax result) anywhere in the questionnaire before or after submitting? Or is it only recorded for HR/the fund? The copy explicitly excludes these values, but nothing is said about showing them on screen.

The AC-01.2.1 example shows the country as '–' for the Switzerland row but 'required' for the Germany row, although the country is always required. Similarly, US-03.3 shows the spouse's date of birth as '–' for Married but 'required' for Registered partnership. Examples elsewhere also mix 'asked' and 'required'. Please correct the example tables so they can be used as test cases.

The trace check notes that the Liechtenstein example treats the employee as 'subject to source tax: yes', while D-007 gives them 'in principle no source tax liability'. What should be recorded for HR as 'subject to source tax' for these employees: yes, no, or a separate status?

uncited_units.text: HR meeting transcript Everyone and everything here is fictional. Anna is the HR manager at Muster AG. Leo works in product at Lonio.
Can you hear me okay? You're a bit quiet.
Is this better? I'm in the small meeting room, the big one is taken. Sorry, let me just close the door.
Much better. So, thanks for making the time. The idea today is simple. We want your new employees to give us everything once, so that you stop chasing them for
Yes, please. Right now it's a mess. I have a Word document, then an Excel file, and then I type everything into the portals by hand. Last month I spent a full a
Okay. And how many people do you hire in a year?
Around twenty. More in summer. We're about a hundred and fifty people now, mostly here in Zurich.
Good. Let's start with the biggest pain. What takes you the most time?
Okay, that's clear. And the questionnaire itself is what?
Great. Do you also want a photo? Some customers ask for one.
It could. Do you want that from day one?
We're with Pensionskasse Muster. They have a portal, it's quite old. I'll send you some screenshots of it after this call, that's easier than me explaining it.
Perfect. What do you need for the fund that you don't have?
Sorry, one second, someone's at my door. [pause] Okay, I'm back, sorry. Where were we?
The Julia story. It doesn't matter.
Right. What else about the employee affects the fund? Are they married, things like that?
And what are the options in that list?
Okay. Noted. Can I go back to source tax? You said all non-Swiss employees.
Sure, send it if it's easy. Do people need anything from you on the first day? Laptops, things like that? I just want to see if that belongs in the same form.
Okay. Anything else on who needs to do it? I'd rather hear all of it now.
Only the timing. When can we have this?
I'll come back to you on that this week, once we've gone through your screenshots.
Good. I'll send them after lunch. Thanks, Leo.

open_questions.question: What should be entered in the pension fund's required 'Canton' field for employees living abroad, and does 'Canton' mean canton of residence or of work?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The field is required and offers only the 26 Swiss cantons; cross-border employees (Germany, Liechtenstein) cannot be registered without a value. Provisionally only residents of Switzerland are asked (D-002).
options: Canton of work (Zurich) for employees abroad
Canton of residence; the fund gives a rule for employees abroad
HR enters a value agreed with the fund
open_questions.recommendation: Domain expert and Pensionskasse Muster to confirm; keep the provisional rule until then.

open_questions.question: How does Pensionskasse Muster want registered partnerships and separated employees registered, and does it want the partner's details?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The fund's list has only Single, Married, Divorced, Widowed. Provisionally registered partnership and separated are entered as Married with the partner's/spouse's date of birth (D-003).
options: Keep the provisional mapping (both as Married)
open_questions.recommendation: Domain expert to verify with the fund.

open_questions.question: Does the fund's form ask for a spouse's date of birth (or other fields) for Divorced or Widowed?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The screenshots show only Single (no) and Married (yes); if the fund needs it for divorced or widowed employees, the registration would be blocked.
open_questions.recommendation: Domain expert to provide a screenshot of the fund screen for these statuses.

open_questions.question: Does Lonio's computed tariff code match the calculator for the paths not explored: the residence block for A/B/H tariffs, more than 3 children, H3N/P3N and the full cross-product of paths?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Lonio now owns the tariff result (D-001); unexplored paths may produce wrong codes. Go-live condition (D-009).
options: Domain expert compares computed codes with the calculator before go-live

open_questions.question: How does a child count in the child-answer combinations that the calculator exploration did not show (rows marked 'Not determined', e.g. married with alternating care where the employee is main contributor; single with an adult child in first education not mainly maintained)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Without these outcomes Lonio cannot compute the tariff code for such employees and the result stays 'cannot be computed yet'.
options: Domain expert runs the missing paths in the calculator and fills the table
Until then, HR determines the code for these cases
open_questions.recommendation: Include these paths in the pre-go-live comparison of D-009.

questions.question: The step notes put the source tax details (denomination, spouse works, children: steps 6/6a) before the cross-border questions (step 7). A Liechtenstein resident who returns daily, or expects at most 45 non-return days, gets 'in principle no source tax liability' and no tariff code. So their denomination, spouse employment and children answers are not needed (AC-05.7.3 shows them as '–'). Should these employees be asked the Liechtenstein questions first and then skip denomination, spouse employment and children? Or are those answers asked and then discarded on submission? Either way the order of the flow changes, and so does what is collected (G-01 data minimisation).

Is the email address typed in for the copy recorded for HR or kept after the email is sent, or only used to send it? Does the copy itself list the 'send me a copy' answer and the email address as submitted answers? The spec says 'nothing more' but does not say whether these two closing items count as answers.

What date checks apply? Can the first working day be in the past, or how far in the future? Is there a minimum or maximum age for the employee's date of birth, and any check on the spouse's date of birth? The ACs only say 'required, DD.MM.YYYY'. A wrong first working day directly gives a wrong insurance start date.

The rule 'How a child counts for the tariff' and the Single-parent H rule say a child counts as an H child when it 'lives in the household and the employee has sole custody or is the main contributor'. Yet row 21 (and AC-06.3.3) count a minor child NOT in the household as an H child (single parent with custody, alternating care, employee is the main contributor → H1N). Which is right: the plain-language rule or the decision table? The H/P letter depends on it.

The certificate of residence question is phrased two ways. information.md asks whether the employee 'has' a certificate; AC-07.2.2 asks whether they 'have provided' it (to HR). Which one is meant? An employee who has the certificate but has not handed it in yet would answer differently, and the answer switches between the cross-border and normal tariff.

The cross-border answers are 'what they expect for the year' / 'in the calendar year'. Which year is meant for an employee who starts late in the year (e.g. in December): the current calendar year, the first full year, or the next 12 months? Without this the question wording cannot be finalised.

For Liechtenstein residents with more than 45 non-return days, the normal code is 'marked subject to the double taxation agreement'. Is this case also flagged for HR, like the 'in principle no liability' case? Or is it only a note on the code? Two different outcomes have to be recorded.
Is there a maximum number of children an employee can enter? The calculator limit is unknown, and the tariff code holds a single digit. What should the result be when 10 or more children count?

For married employees, 'Has children' includes the spouse's/partner's children. For a stepchild, whose custody, maintenance contribution and 'other parent' do the custody and contribution questions refer to? The question wording has to make this clear, or answers will be inconsistent.
HR words the permit reminder. Who supplies the final text, and by when? It also has to work for Swiss citizens living abroad. Without the text the story cannot be finished or accepted.

Before submission, can the employee leave the questionnaire and come back later with their answers kept? Is there a deadline, or a point at which an unsubmitted questionnaire's answers are deleted? 'Kept while going back and forth' does not say whether answers survive across sessions, which matters for data minimisation.

Should the employee see the derived insurance start date (or the source tax result) anywhere in the questionnaire before or after submitting? Or is it only recorded for HR/the fund? The copy explicitly excludes these values, but nothing is said about showing them on screen.

The AC-01.2.1 example shows the country as '–' for the Switzerland row but 'required' for the Germany row, although the country is always required. Similarly, US-03.3 shows the spouse's date of birth as '–' for Married but 'required' for Registered partnership. Examples elsewhere also mix 'asked' and 'required'. Please correct the example tables so they can be used as test cases.

The trace check notes that the Liechtenstein example treats the employee as 'subject to source tax: yes', while D-007 gives them 'in principle no source tax liability'. What should be recorded for HR as 'subject to source tax' for these employees: yes, no, or a separate status?

review.summary: All example simulations pass, and none of the 5 open questions is blocking. The package is still not ready for four reasons. Decision D-036 has new evidence and must be re-confirmed (the check report lists this as an error). The written H-child rule and the decision table give different answers. The Liechtenstein status is inconsistent and its question order is unclear. Four technical or unsourced behaviours have leaked into the stories. Fix these and the package should reach ready_with_caveats. The caveats would be the open questions for the pension fund and D-009: before go-live, a domain expert compares Lonio's tariff codes with the calculator.

findings.title: D-036 has new evidence and needs re-confirming
findings.why: The decision on the emailed copy was made before Anna's email arrived. The email says the copy holds only the submitted answers, exactly as submitted, with no derived values. Until D-036 is re-confirmed, US-08.4 rests on an outdated decision.
findings.action: Check D-036 against the email, then confirm, update or drop it, and run `pipeline reconfirm D-036`. Resolve this together with finding 6.

findings.title: H-child rule text contradicts the decision table
findings.why: The written rule says an H child must live in the employee's household. Row 21 and AC-06.3.3 count a child outside the household as an H child (H1N). This changes the tariff letter (H/P vs A/L), so the computed code would be wrong in one of the two readings.
findings.evidence: dev_refinement major (feature.md H rule vs row 21 / AC-06.3.3); trace_judge rule.single_parent_h_tariff, item.has_children, item.child_main_financial_contributor
findings.action: Add a decision to decisions.yaml saying which is right. The calculator run in F-c2faa7 supports the table. Then align the rule text and cite the facts behind it (c78e0c, 562299, 97139a).

findings.title: Liechtenstein residents: status and question order undefined
findings.why: The US-01.3 example records 'subject to source tax: yes' with no source tax questions. D-007 instead asks the questions and can give 'in principle no liability'. Denomination, spouse and children answers are asked before the cross-border questions but are not needed for these employees, which goes against data minimisation (G-01).
findings.evidence: trace_judge story.US-01.3; dev_refinement major (feature.md steps 6/6a vs 7); info US-01.3, US-05.7 (>45 days double-taxation-agreement flag)
findings.action: Decide what is recorded as 'subject to source tax' for Liechtenstein residents (yes, no, or a separate status). Decide whether the Liechtenstein questions come first and the later ones are skipped. Decide whether the >45-days case is flagged for HR.

findings.title: US-05.7 adds 'cannot be computed yet' behaviour that no source asked for
findings.why: The spec chooses one fallback for unexplored child combinations, but OQ-child-paths-undetermined still lists 'HR determines the code' as an option. Engineering would build an outcome nobody has agreed to.
findings.evidence: tech_leak US-05.7; trace_judge story.US-05.6 (AC-05.6.4), story.US-05.7 (AC-05.7.5), rule.source_tax_result

findings.title: US-08.3 widens 'no history kept' to every derived value
findings.why: This is a data-retention decision. D-033 covers only the first working day. The story also cites a 'Julia changed start date' incident that no source backs.
findings.action: Either narrow the wording to what D-033 says, or add a decision that covers all derived results. Remove the unbacked incident or cite a source for it.

findings.title: Emailed copy: retention of the email address and scope of 'answers' unclear
findings.why: Nothing says whether the email address typed in for the copy is stored or shown to HR. Nothing says whether the 'send me a copy' answer and the address count as answers that appear in the copy. AC-08.4.3 lists excluded derived values that no source names.
findings.evidence: dev_refinement major US-08.4; trace_judge rule.employee_copy_content, story.US-08.4; inferred item.copy_email_address
findings.action: While re-confirming D-036, decide how long the address is kept and what exactly the copy contains. Write AC-08.4.3 as 'no derived values' rather than an unsourced list.

findings.title: No date checks for the first working day or dates of birth
findings.why: A wrong first working day leads straight to a wrong insurance start date for the pension fund. Engineering cannot write validation without rules.
findings.action: Ask HR and decide: can the first working day be in the past, and how far ahead can it be? Are there age limits for the employee's date of birth, and any check on the spouse's date of birth?

findings.title: Implementation and UI wording in the business rules
findings.why: The text refers to 'the expression', and US-06.1 describes add/remove child controls. These are design and implementation choices, not requirements.
findings.evidence: tech_leak feature.md ('The expression evaluates one child…'); tech_leak US-06.1
findings.action: Rewrite as business rules: 'each child is assessed separately; the counted children are added up' and 'answers are collected for each child'. Leave the UI to design.

findings.why: Several rows (for example 'other country → base tariff' and 'not subject → no result') rest on facts the rule does not cite. That breaks the link from rule to source.
